findings.F1: Request-side Jackson binding differs fundamentally from response-side serialization: references bind absent≡null (mirrored by .nullable().default(null) — .nullish() is WRONG on request bodies, it invents an undefined state Java never has); primitives take JVM defaults on absence but REJECT explicit null (coercion failure → 400). Recorded as the canonical request-side convention for all future contracts tasks.
findings.F2: Jackson's default scalar coercions are part of the Java accept set on JSON bodies — mirrored via javaJsonInt/javaJsonDouble/javaJsonBool ("3"→3, "1e3"→1000 integral-only, "0x10"/"10.5"/"" rejected, "true"/"false" text binds).
findings.F3: TeacherCurriculumController has 5 write endpoints (POST /drafts, /nodes/{id}/validate, /nodes/{id}/reject, /versions/{id}/validate, /versions/{id}/archive) that PR #20's 501 inventory did NOT list (it covers /teacher/content only) — the write-surfaces follow-up task must scope them in.
findings.F4: Verified read-only controllers: CurriculumController, ContentReaderController, QuestionAssetController (zero write mappings) — write-flow contract surface is exactly ContentController + ContentDocumentController + TeacherCurriculumController.
findings.F5: CanonicalDocumentValidator's P-6 documentId derivation (SHA-256 over 'sha256:<checksum>|engine:<engine>|version:<engineVersion>', stripped+lowercased, UUIDv5 nibble/variant) is ported byte-exact with independently computed vectors; the v2 ingest route MUST enforce it or consumer dedup breaks silently.

Mirrored as exported constants + the violations collector — NOT folded into the binding schemas.
